execution-metadata-and-vars._why: the additionalKeys half of the sandbox: $execution (id/mode/urls), $vars, the deprecated aliases, and $execution.customData driving execution-metadata. Probes are ORDER-DEPENDENT on purpose: set() then get() must be recorded and replayed in the same sequence. Duplicate probe paths collapse in the golden dict, so each path appears once: getAll is read only after the writes.

orphan-branch-default._why: A node that HAS run data but is not connected to the active node: `$('Code')` must fall back to branchIndex 0, the reference's default for an unconnected source. The `$()` getters compute `getNodeConnectionIndexes(active, node)?.sourceIndex ?? 0`, and a mutation of that default is invisible unless the referenced node has MORE THAN ONE output branch — hence main[0] and main[1] carry different items here.

pinned-and-disabled-node._why: ISSUE-016 follow-up, settled by the oracle instead of by argument: does the data proxy honour `disabled` when it substitutes pinned output? `grep -n disabled packages/workflow/src/workflow-data-proxy.ts` returns NOTHING, while `NodeHelpers.getNodeParametersIssues` (node-helpers.ts:1211) and the execution loop both branch on it. So the proxy layer and the execution layer are allowed to disagree, and the recorded values here are what a port of `$()` must reproduce.

pinned-upstream-substitutes-input._why: workflow-data-proxy.ts:909-926 — getTaskData() falls back to pinDataToTask(), which FABRICATES an ITaskData ({data:{main:[pinData]}, startTime:0, executionTime:0, executionIndex:0, source:[]}) for the previous node when run data is missing, so pinned upstream output reaches $input although NOTHING executed. Two halves are recorded: with a source present the substitution is visible, and with executeData.source absent $input raises 'No execution data available' instead of answering empty. connectionInputData stays empty so the substitution cannot be confused with real input.

input-placeholder-sourcing-edge._why: The reference derives $input's guard from `placeholdersDataInputData`, NOT from the length of connectionInputData: workflow-data-proxy.ts:1061-1079 takes runData[active][runIndex].inputOverride when the ACTIVE node already has run data, and connectionInputData[runIndex].json otherwise, then throws 'No execution data available' when that placeholder object is falsy. A port that only checks `connectionInputData.length === 0` therefore answers where the reference raises — an item with binary and no json is enough to diverge.
